The attention mechanism confirms that the inferred parameters are driven by physically meaningful abundance signatures. By unifying amortized parameter inference, Bayesian model comparison, and interpretability in a single probabilistic framework, compass provides a scalable approach for precision chemical evolution studies with current and forthcoming spectroscopic surveys.

articles.title: Mass-conservative voxelisation of smoothed particles using cumulative kernels
articles.abstract: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations are frequently post-processed on Cartesian grids for applications such as radiative transfer calculations, visualisation, and data analysis. While numerous voxelisation algorithms have been proposed, relatively little attention has been paid to the fundamental properties that such algorithms should satisfy. We argue that SPH voxelisation algorithms should accurately reproduce the underlying density field, conserve mass globally, remain consistent under grid refinement, and be computationally efficient. We present a new finite-volume algorithm designed to satisfy these requirements simultaneously. Starting from a finite-volume formulation of the SPH density field, we derive a simple expression for the mass contained in a Cartesian voxel in terms of a cumulative kernel function. The cumulative kernel is tabulated numerically once for any compact-support smoothing kernel, independently of its analytical form, so that the same tabulation and voxelisation machinery applies unchanged to any such kernel. During voxelisation, the mass contributions are obtained from interpolated evaluations of this precomputed function at voxel corners, with values at corners shared by neighbouring voxels evaluated only once and reused. We compare the new cumulative-kernel algorithm to nearest-grid-point assignment, centre sampling, regular subsampling, and Monte Carlo integration, using direct high-order numerical integration as a reference for the voxel densities, and implement it in the 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer code SKIRT. The cumulative-kernel algorithm reproduces the reference voxel densities substantially more accurately than the sampling-based methods considered. articles.title: Demographic dynamics of the Japanese astronomy and astrophysics publication community during 1996-2025
articles.abstract: We investigate the demographic evolution of the Japanese astronomy and astrophysics publication community during 1996-2025 using bibliometric data from 23,274 publications in major journals in the field. The number of active Japan-affiliated authors increased from approximately 600 in the late 1990s to more than 2,000 by the early 2020s, while annual publication output reached approximately 1,400 by 2025. Participation was highly heterogeneous, with 46% of authors observed in only one publication year within the study period and a smaller core showing long observed participation periods. We define the Community Renewal Rate (CRR) as a community-level measure of renewal, calculated as the fraction of active authors not observed during a specified preceding interval. The 5-year CRR typically remained near one quarter of the active community, with annual values ranging from approximately 21% to 33%, indicating persistent renewal despite substantial community growth. An order-of-magnitude comparison suggests that newly entering students account for only part of the renewal-author population. The community therefore expanded while sustaining both continuity through authors with long observed participation periods and renewal through recurring changes in active membership.

articles.title: Mining the time axis with TRON. IV. MeerKAT detects a radio burst from a nearby M~dwarf
articles.abstract: We report the detection of a minute-timescale, highly circularly polarised ($\sim100\%$) radio burst from an active M dwarf (spectral type M1Ve), PM J14111$-$6155, located 19.6 pc from the Sun. Identified in the 1.28 GHz SMGPS using 8-second integrations from the TRON-pipeline, the burst peaked at 7.7 mJy. Visibility-based dynamic spectra reveal a drifting, band-limited emission feature ($\sim$300 MHz FWHM) with a maximum cut-off near 1.65 GHz, associated with electron cyclotron maser instability (ECMI), implying the existence of large-scale magnetic topologies ($B_* \approx 0.59$ kG). A non-detection ($3σ$ upper limit) four hours later points to intermittent or rotationally modulated beamed emission. An analysis of both TESS and ground-based survey data failed to recover an unambiguous rotational period for the optical counterpart. Follow-up SALT spectroscopy confirms its active chromospheric state, exhibiting prominent emission in the Ca {\sc ii} infrared triplet, Balmer lines, and persistent double-peaked H$α$ emission ($44.6\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ peak separation) attributable to optically thick self-absorption. This discovery demonstrates that the coordinated use of time-series optical photometry, high-resolution spectroscopy, and high-cadence spectropolarimetric radio imaging enables direct probing of coherent radio emission from the magnetically active atmospheres of nearby M dwarfs.

articles.title: Why supersonic UAP events are not accompanied by acoustic booms?
articles.abstract: The Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) events have been recorded for decades. However, the nature of these events remains unknown. We advocate an idea that the dark matter (DM) in form of the axion quark nuggets (AQN) made of standard model quarks (or {\it antiquarks}) and gluons could {\it simultaneously} explain many observed puzzling features which always accompany the UAP events, such as high velocity, enormous acceleration, absence of any remaining materials in affected area, etc. This long list of mysterious features also includes the absence of any sound which normally accompanies any supersonic motion. The AQN framework answers this last puzzle as well, which represents the title of the present work. The AQN dark matter model was invented long ago without any intension to apply the model to UAP events. Rather, it was invented with a single motivation to explain the observed similarity $Ω_{\rm DM}\sim Ω_{\rm visible}$ between visible and DM components, which represents a very generic feature of this framework, not sensitive to any parameters of the construction. In this work we use the same framework with the same set of parameters to study the observed UAP events. Essentially we argue that a specific class of UAP represents the close cousin of other mysteries known for decades (even centuries), such as sky-quakes, Ball Lightnings, and Mysterious Transient events. In other words, the UAPs represent different manifestations of exactly the same objects, the AQNs propagating in atmosphere. The fuel powering all these mysterious energetic events is one and the same: it is the antiquark core of the AQNs. We also present some suggestions on type of instruments required to study this specific (and well defined) type of the UAP events.
